documents.text:
Expression of concern: Dose-response of iron supplementation on fatigue

The editors have received concerns about the calculation of the dose-response analysis in this article and are investigating.

Retraction and replacement: Dose-response of iron supplementation on fatigue

Following the editors' investigation, this article is retracted and replaced by a corrected version (doi 10.9999/fake.2019.011v2). The dose-response slope in Table 3 was miscalculated: it was reported as 0.45 points per 10 mg and the correct value is 0.28 points per 10 mg. The finding that iron supplementation reduces fatigue is unchanged.

evaluation.change_summary: The editors issued an expression of concern because they had received concerns about the calculation of the dose-response analysis and were investigating, and after that investigation the article was retracted and replaced by a corrected version. The dose-response slope in Table 3 was miscalculated: the original paper reported a slope of 0.45 points per 10 mg with a 95% CI of 0.30 to 0.60, while the corrected version reports 0.28 points per 10 mg with a 95% CI of 0.15 to 0.41. The notice states that the finding that iron supplementation reduces fatigue is unchanged, and the corrected version still concludes that the reduction in fatigue increased with the daily dose between 20 and 60 mg. The correction changes the size of the dose-response effect, but the direction of the finding stands.
evaluation.evaluation: In the Discussion, your draft compares its estimated slope of 0.41 fatigue points per 10 mg with the 0.45 per 10 mg of Park and Singh [7], and says this closeness supports the validity of its design. The stored paper reports a dose-response slope of 0.45 points per 10 mg (95% CI 0.30 to 0.60) in Table 3, but the retraction-and-replacement notice says that slope was miscalculated and the correct value is 0.28. The corrected version reports a slope of 0.28 points per 10 mg with a 95% CI of 0.15 to 0.41. Your Discussion comparison uses the 0.45 value that the correction changes to 0.28, so this use is touched, while the notice states that the finding that iron supplementation reduces fatigue is unchanged. Because the touched use is a comparison and the change is of medium severity, the impact on your draft is low.
evaluation.recommendation: In the Discussion, your draft compares its estimated slope of 0.41 fatigue points per 10 mg with the 0.45 per 10 mg of Park and Singh [7], and says this closeness supports the validity of its design. After the editors' investigation, the article was retracted and replaced by a corrected version, and the notice says the slope in Table 3 was miscalculated: it was reported as 0.45 points per 10 mg, and the correct value is 0.28. The corrected version reports 0.28 points per 10 mg with a 95% CI of 0.15 to 0.41, so your Discussion comparison uses the 0.45 value that the correction changes to 0.28. The notice states that the finding that iron supplementation reduces fatigue is unchanged, and the corrected version still concludes that the reduction in fatigue increased with the daily dose between 20 and 60 mg. Update the number in that Discussion sentence and cite the corrected version and the notice instead of the original. Then recheck whether your slope can still be called close to theirs and still supports your design, and reword or hedge that claim if not.
